definition: Hierarchical Risk Parity (HRP) is an advanced investment portfolio optimization framework developed in 2016 by Marcos López de Prado.
details: HRP is a probabilistic graph-based alternative to the prevailing mean-variance optimization (MVO) framework developed by Harry Markowitz. HRP algorithms apply discrete mathematics and machine learning techniques to create diversified and robust investment portfolios that outperform MVO methods out-of-sample. HRP aims to address the limitations of traditional portfolio construction methods, particularly when dealing with highly correlated assets. Following its publication, HRP has been implemented in numerous open-source libraries, and received multiple extensions.

explainer.lead: Hierarchical Risk Parity is a portfolio optimization framework developed in 2016 by Marcos López de Prado, a graph-based alternative to mean-variance optimization. It matters because it aims to build diversified, robust portfolios that outperform MVO out-of-sample, especially with highly correlated assets.

tiers.eli5: Instead of splitting your money by staring at every pair of investments at once, you group similar ones together and spread money across the groups, so no single cluster dominates.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it to allocate weights when assets are highly correlated and mean-variance inputs are unstable. A pitfall is that it depends on the clustering and distance choices, so results vary with those design decisions.
tiers.paperLevel: HRP is a probabilistic graph-based alternative to mean-variance optimization that applies discrete mathematics and machine learning techniques to construct diversified, robust portfolios, aiming to address limitations of traditional methods with highly correlated assets; the given definition supplies no explicit formula.

explainer.example: For a set of highly correlated assets, an HRP algorithm clusters them and allocates weights across the hierarchy, producing a portfolio that outperforms MVO out-of-sample.
